name: Lednice-Valtice
tagline: A vast landscaped garden shared by two fairy-tale chateaux, at the heart of Moravia's rolling wine country.
highlight: Cycling a quiet lane between vineyard villages, stopping at a family-run cellar for wine poured by the person who actually made it.
shortDescription: A vast UNESCO-listed landscaped garden shared by two fairy-tale chateaux, Lednice and Valtice, at the heart of Moravia's wine country.
metaDescription: A Lednice-Valtice travel guide: Lednice Chateau, the Minaret, Valtice Chateau, Moravian wine tasting, food and how to plan a visit.
nearestAirport: Brno–Tuřany Airport (BRQ), about 45 minutes by road
knownFor: Lednice Chateau, the Minaret, Moravian wine country
budget: Kč1,800–3,500 per day, budget to mid-range
intro: Lednice-Valtice is genuinely one of Europe's largest deliberately landscaped areas, a UNESCO-listed cultural landscape connecting two aristocratic chateaux across 200 square kilometres of parkland and vineyards.
Its genuinely fairy-tale centrepiece is Lednice Chateau, a neo-Gothic palace surrounded by an English-style park scattered with follies, including a striking Ottoman-style minaret.
The wider region is genuinely also the heart of Moravian wine country, a landscape of rolling vineyards and small villages built around family-run wine cellars.

whyVisit.intro: Lednice-Valtice's case rests genuinely on an extraordinary landscaped estate paired with the best of Moravian wine country.

points.title: Lednice Chateau is genuinely a fairy-tale palace
points.text: A neo-Gothic showpiece surrounded by one of Europe's largest English-style landscaped parks.

points.title: The Minaret is genuinely a delightful surprise
points.text: A 60-metre Ottoman-style tower rising incongruously from the Moravian countryside.

points.title: It's genuinely the heart of Moravian wine country
points.text: Rolling vineyards and village cellars producing wine most visitors never expect to find in the Czech Republic.

points.title: The scale is genuinely built for slow exploration
points.text: Cycling paths connect the chateaux, follies and surrounding wine villages.

points.title: It works genuinely well as a Brno day trip or overnight stay
points.text: Close enough for a day, rewarding enough to justify staying longer.

attractionsIntro: The region's essential sights are genuinely spread across two chateaux, their shared parkland and the surrounding vineyards.

attractions.name: Lednice Chateau

image.alt: Lednice Chateau, a neo-Gothic palace in South Moravia

attractions.text: Genuinely the region's fairy-tale centrepiece, a neo-Gothic palace remodelled in the 19th century for the powerful Liechtenstein family.
attractions.tip: Genuinely book the interior tour ahead in summer — time slots do sell out.

attractions.name: The Lednice Minaret

image.alt: The Ottoman-style Minaret in Lednice's park

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the park's most surprising follies, a 60-metre Ottoman-style tower with a viewing platform at the top.
attractions.tip: Genuinely climb it for one of the best views over the entire landscaped park.

attractions.name: The Lednice Castle Gardens

image.alt: The landscaped gardens at Lednice Chateau

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the largest English-style landscaped parks in Europe, dotted with follies, temples and a glasshouse.
attractions.tip: Genuinely rent a bicycle to properly cover the park's scale.

attractions.name: Valtice Chateau
attractions.text: Genuinely the Liechtenstein family's former main residence, a grand baroque chateau at the estate's southern end.
attractions.tip: Genuinely pair a visit with the Salon of Wines in the chateau's cellars, showcasing the country's best vintages.

attractions.name: The Reistna Colonnade
attractions.text: Genuinely a grand neoclassical colonnade on a hilltop near Valtice, built purely as a scenic folly with sweeping views.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a rewarding short walk or cycle from Valtice itself.

attractions.name: The surrounding vineyards

image.file: File:View of vineyards from Slunečná observation tower 2020 02.jpg
image.alt: Vineyards in the wine country around Lednice-Valtice

attractions.text: Genuinely the backbone of the local economy, rolling vineyard hills scattered with small wine-producing villages.
attractions.tip: Genuinely several villages have observation towers offering a wide view over the vineyard landscape.

attractions.name: The pond in Lednice's park

image.alt: A pond in the landscaped park at Lednice

attractions.text: Genuinely a peaceful spot within the wider park, reflecting the surrounding follies and mature trees.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a lovely stop partway around a longer park walk or cycle.

thingsToDoIntro: The region genuinely rewards slow travel, best covered by bicycle between its chateaux and wine villages.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Lednice Chateau's interior

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential visit, taking in the chateau's ornately carved neo-Gothic interiors.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely several different tour routes cover different parts of the chateau — pick based on your interest and time.

thingsToDo.title: Climb the Minaret for the view

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding short climb, with sweeping views over the park and surrounding countryside.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine with a chateau visit — both sit within the same park.

thingsToDo.title: Walk or cycle the Castle Gardens

image.alt: Walking through the landscaped gardens at Lednice

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to spend a few hours, exploring the park's follies, glasshouse and quiet paths.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a bicycle covers the park's scale far more comfortably than walking alone.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Valtice Chateau

image.alt: Touring Valtice Chateau in South Moravia

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely worthwhile stop, the Liechtenstein family's grander baroque residence at the estate's other end.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine with a wine tasting at the Salon of Wines in the chateau's cellars.

thingsToDo.title: Cycle the wine trails between villages

image.file: File:Tent in vineyards near Velké Pavlovice 2020.jpg

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely lovely way to spend an afternoon, pedalling quiet lanes between vineyard villages.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely well-marked wine trails connect several villages worth stopping in along the way.

thingsToDo.title: Taste wine at a village cellar

image.alt: A traditional wine cellar in South Moravia

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential regional experience, tasting local wine directly from the family that produced it.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely many cellars welcome walk-ins, though calling ahead for a proper tasting is worth the effort.

Genuinely warm and lively, with vineyards at their most lush.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Lednice-Valtice visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Rent genuinely a bicycle on arrival — the estate's scale genuinely rewards it.
Book genuinely chateau interior tours ahead in peak summer season.
Call genuinely ahead for a proper wine cellar tasting rather than just walking in.
Pack genuinely a picnic for the park — options inside are limited compared to the villages.
Visit genuinely in September or October for the region's wine harvest season.
Base yourself genuinely in Brno if you'd rather day-trip than stay locally.

faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it's one of Europe's largest landscaped cultural sites, and the heart of the country's wine-producing region.

faq.q: How do you get to Lednice-Valtice?
faq.a: Genuinely easiest from Brno by bus or car, taking under an hour; from Prague it's a longer trip via Břeclav.

faq.q: How many days do you need?
faq.a: One day genuinely covers Lednice Chateau and its park; two days allows Valtice and proper wine tasting time too.

faq.q: Is this a good destination for non-drinkers?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — the chateaux, park follies and cycling routes are all worthwhile without any wine tasting at all.

faq.q: Do you need a car to visit?
faq.a: No, genuinely not — a bicycle covers the core area well, though a car helps for more distant wine villages.

faq.q: Can you combine this with Brno?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely easily — it's a natural day trip or overnight add-on to a Brno-based Moravia itinerary.
